**0.11.0 is a breaking release.** It counts usage per stream version and moves the storage and protocol format to format epoch 7. A 0.11 node refuses epoch-6 Raft WAL directories and object-storage prefixes at startup and refuses 0.10 peers, and a 0.10 node refuses 0.11 peers. The backup format stays 5, so `ursulactl restore` of 0.11 restores a 0.10 backup. There is no in-place upgrade, no rolling upgrade and no rollback.

- **If you cannot move your data yet, stay on 0.10.1.**
- **Deploy 0.11 fresh and move your data with a backup.** Install 0.11 on empty PVCs and never-used object-storage prefixes for the cold store and S3 snapshots, with the 0.10 cluster's `server.cluster_id` and `raft.group_count`. Stop client writes and every SQLite session, back up 0.10 with `ursulactl backup-create` and `backup-verify` of 0.10, stop the 0.10 nodes, copy their cold objects into the 0.11 cold root, skipping `URSULA_FORMAT_EPOCH` and `snapshots/`, and run `ursulactl restore` of 0.11, which checks the copy first. Every restored stream answers with a new `Stream-Incarnation`.
- **`helm upgrade` from 0.10 stops at the first pod**, which finds the 0.10 data on its volume and exits. Recover with `helm rollback`. Keep the peer lists of 0.10 and 0.11 nodes apart.
- **The gateway gives a request time for its size** ([#891](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/891)). `ursulagw` waits for a node's answer for `--response-header-timeout` plus the time the node needs to store or copy the request's bytes at 8 MiB per second: its body, or the parts a snapshot commit copies. A large append, create, snapshot or commit no longer gets `504` while the node still works on it. The VFS waits the same allowance beyond its own 15 s, which counts a commit's parts the same way, so it gives up after any gateway in front of the node. An object store slower than 8 MiB per second still needs a higher `--response-header-timeout` (`gateway.responseHeaderTimeoutSeconds`).
- **Usage is counted per stream version.** Each stream version holds its committed counters and applied appends in replicated state, and `/__ursula/usage` derives each bucket's counters from them, with the version 2 shape and values. A deleted, expired or purged stream leaves an end record with its final usage, at most 65,536 per group. Group snapshots carry each stream version's usage and the end records, and an install requires every bucket's counters to equal those parts, so a replica that installs a snapshot keeps them. A restore refuses a backup that holds a stream but no history event, which no release since 0.8 writes. `/__ursula/metrics` gains `usage_end_records_retired` and `usage_end_records_folded_early`, and `group_state_gauges` the end-record gauges. `ursula_runtime::AppendResponse` loses `stream_append_count`, `GroupSnapshot` replaces `stream_append_counts` with `usage`, and `GroupEngine::purge_bucket` takes a `PurgeBucketRequest`.
- **Per-stream usage export.** `POST /__ursula/usage/streams` on the admin listener lists, per Raft group, the usage of each stream version that changed after a cursor, with its counters, its gauges while it lives and how it ended, and relists a group with each bucket's retired usage and totals when the cursor needs it. A metering consumer follows the contract in [Per-stream usage](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#per-stream-usage). `history` in the backup import answer is 16 lowercase hex digits, as in the export, where it was a JSON number, and the purge report names in `groups` each group's purge entry and the history it applied in. After the move, check that each bucket's counters in `/__ursula/usage` equal the last 0.10 report's, and start a metering consumer from cursor `start` once `ursulactl restore` has finished.
- **End records fold in the background sweep, and `raft.deleted_data_max_age` has a higher floor.** Each group's leader folds an end record into its bucket's counters half of `raft.deleted_data_max_age` after the removal, by its own monotonic clock, with the `Sweep` Raft entries that replace `ExpireStreams`. The sweep runs every minute, or every sixteenth of the bound if that is shorter. The bound must leave room for an end record to leave within it: with the default install timeout of 120 seconds, a value set below 980 seconds with an S3 snapshot store, or 964 seconds inline, refuses to start with `DeletedDataMaxAgeTooShort`. The default of one hour is unchanged. A node that restarts or installs a snapshot dates the end records it holds then by their removal times, so keep the nodes' clocks in sync. The bound's functions move from `RaftConfig` to `UrsulaConfig`, and `TidyStreamsRequest` gains `deleted_data_max_age`.
- **`ursula_stream::MAX_COLD_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` and its `ursula_runtime` re-export are removed.** Use `ursula_headers::MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`, the same 1 GiB.
- **A bucket purge removes its streams in stream-id order**, so every replica of a group numbers the purge's cold-object cleanup entries alike, and cold GC reclaims every purged stream's objects after a leader change. 0.10.1 has the same issue: on 0.10, repeat a purge until it reports `cold_gc_complete=true`.
- **Upgrade the SQLite extension with the server, and stop every SQLite session before the move.** `Ursula-Protocol` now carries the server's release line, `11`, where 0.8 to 0.10 sent `2`. The 0.11 extension refuses a server of another line with `protocol_mismatch` at open and at import, and an answer without `Ursula-Protocol` and `Ursula-Cluster-Id` with `no_server_identity`. Both replace `server_too_old`. A bound 0.11 session checks the line only at its next `HEAD`, which it sends to confirm an answer such as a `412` or a `404`, so it may keep writing to a cluster moved to another line under it. The 0.8 to 0.10 extensions refuse a 0.11 server at once with `server_too_old`, but a running 0.10 session checks only the cluster id, so it does not notice the move by itself.

Every change is listed in the [0.11.0 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#0110), and installing 0.11.0 is described in [Upgrading to 0.11](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#upgrading-to-011).
